chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The believer has greater sanctity/honor than the Ka'ba.
ai.seo_question: What is the sanctity of a believer compared to the Ka'ba?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s declaration that the honor of a believer surpasses even that of the Ka'ba, highlighting the ontological elevation of the faithful through divine grace. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on the spiritual status of the *Mu'min* as a vessel of divine knowledge and virtue, often interpreted as indicating that while the Ka'ba is a physical sanctuary, the believer is a living sanctuary of God's attributes.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-95 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Hammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Umar that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
A believer’s honor is more than that of the Ka’ba.”
